# @rootnative/impulse

> Declarative gesture primitives for React Native, built on
> react-native-gesture-handler. One hook per intent. Hooks return shared values
> and a gesture; Impulse starts no animation and ships no components.

Status: 0.0.0-alpha.0. Eight intents ship. A device sweep on an Android
emulator and an iOS simulator drove every intent. It proves mechanics, not
feel, so every default below is still a design intention.

Docs: https://rootnative.github.io/impulse/
Full: https://rootnative.github.io/impulse/llms-full.txt
Source: https://github.com/rootnative/impulse

## Install

npm install @rootnative/impulse

Peers: react, react-native, react-native-gesture-handler,
react-native-reanimated, react-native-worklets. Render a
<GestureHandlerRootView> above any component using a gesture — if it is
missing, gestures never fire and nothing warns.

## What ships

useTap, useDoubleTap, useLongPress, useDrag, usePan, useSwipe, usePinch,
useRotate — intent hooks. useGestures — composition. useRawGesture — the
escape hatch. GestureDetector is re-exported from the package entry.

NOT IMPLEMENTED, do not import: useHover, useEdgeSwipe.
They are designed only.

usePan and useDrag are not synonyms. useDrag owns a position: x and y
accumulate across gestures and bounds clamps them. usePan owns nothing: it
reports translation, velocity, and a per-frame change the consumer adds up,
and it zeroes at every gesture.

useSwipe is a pan judged at release. directions is also the activation
criterion — an all-horizontal list gives a directional threshold, so the
swipe shares a view with a vertical scroller with no relation declared.

usePinch owns a scale that accumulates across gestures, so min and max are
the viewer's zoom range, not one gesture's. focal is the midpoint between the
fingers and the point the zoom must happen about — scaling about the view's
centre slides the content out from under them. It has NO activation criteria:
RNGH's pinch exposes no threshold, so a pinch and a pan are separated by a
relation alone — useGestures([pinch, pan], { mode: 'simultaneous' }).

useRotate reports DEGREES, not the radians RNGH reports. This is the one
place Impulse changes a unit: min: -45, not -Math.PI / 4. It applies to
angle, gestureAngle, velocity and the min/max range. The angle accumulates
and does NOT wrap — a second full turn reports 720. anchor is the point the
turn happens about, the counterpart of pinch's focal. It has NO activation
criteria either, so rotate and pinch are composed simultaneous.

Subpaths: @rootnative/impulse/{tap,double-tap,long-press,drag,pan,swipe,pinch,rotate,compose,raw,gesture-handler}

## The shape of every hook

const tap = useTap({ onTap: select })
tap.gesture    // hand to <GestureDetector>
tap.ref        // name it in another hook's alongside / blocks / deferTo
tap.isActive   // SharedValue<boolean>

useDrag adds x and y, both SharedValue<number>, both writable, both
accumulating across gestures.

## Threads — the callback name states the thread

JS thread: onTap, onDoubleTap, onLongPress, onLongPressEnd, onDragStart,
onDragEnd. Ordinary functions; Impulse owns the runOnJS boundary.

Worklets: onBegin, onUpdate, onFinalize. Mark with 'worklet'. They are direct
gesture dependencies, so keep their identity stable — an inline worklet
rebuilds the gesture every render. An inline JS-thread callback does not.

## Composition

useGestures(members, { mode }) where mode is race | simultaneous | exclusive.
A composed result is itself a member. Precedence reads left to right.

A tap and a double tap are exclusive with the double tap FIRST, never race — a
single tap recognizes on first release and would win every race. The composed
single tap then pays maxDelay in latency.

useGestures does not accept coexistence options. Put them on the members.

## Coexistence

alongside -> both recognize          (simultaneousWithExternalGesture)
blocks    -> this gesture wins       (blocksExternalGesture)
deferTo   -> the named gesture wins  (requireExternalGestureToFail)

Name another hook's .ref, not its .gesture.

TRAP: a relation target must carry a handlerTag. React Native's ScrollView has
none, so the relation is SILENTLY dropped on every platform. Use
gesture-handler's ScrollView / FlatList, from @rootnative/impulse/gesture-handler.

TRAP: a component ref needs `as unknown as GestureReference`. RNGH types the
target as a ref to a component type, which is not what ref={} produces.

## Defaults

useTap: pointers 1, maxDuration 500ms, maxDistance 10pt
useDoubleTap: same, plus maxDelay 500ms (probably too generous; 250-300 is
  closer to what platforms use)
useLongPress: minDuration 500ms, maxDistance 10pt
useDrag: axis both, threshold 10pt, elastic 0, unbounded

## isActive does not mean the same thing in every hook

useTap sets it at touch-down — a real pressed state.
useLongPress and useDrag set it at recognition.

## Known gaps a consumer can hit

- No JS-thread callback for a cancelled gesture. Every intent callback is
  guarded on success; onFinalize is the only cancel-aware one and it is a
  worklet.
- useLongPress maxDistance cancels an ACTIVE press on web, against RNGH's own
  documented contract. Hold-then-drag does not work there at the default.
- A missing <GestureHandlerRootView> fails silently and Impulse cannot warn.
- Web is surveyed by hand; no jsdom test pins any of it.

## Out of scope, by decision

No components. No animation vocabulary, springs or easing. No haptics policy.
useDrag returns values and no style — @rootnative/inertia-gestures has a
useDrag that returns an animatedStyle and requires @rootnative/inertia.
